text:
alex: Quick sync — planning the API evolution handshake. Proposal: introduce an Accept-Version / Accept header that opts clients into v2 behavior, keep /v1 routing for a 90-day deprecation runway. Need owners for SDK bump, infra routing, docs, and QA.

mira: I can own SDK release (py + js). ETA for PRs?

dan: I’ll own infra-side: header routing, fallback logic, and canary gating. Need a small canary cluster for header negotiation tests.

katie: Can we avoid breaking webhook consumers? We still have integrations that assume current payloads.

alex: Good call @katie — plan: preserve v1 payload schema for 90 days and require explicit opt-in for new fields via Accept-Version: v2.

mira: SDK plan: target 3.1.0. Default client behavior will remain v1 unless configured to opt-in; include a convenience flag to opt into v2. PRs: #5422 (python), #5423 (js). @devex can you draft the release notes?

devex: Yup, will draft. Also adding a short code sample + migration diff. Quick sample I'll drop here: 
```
curl -H \"Accept-Version: v2\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.ai/generate
```
JS: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ acceptVersion: 'v2' })
await client.generate(...)
```
Use these in the migration guide.

dan: Infra checklist (high level):
- router: header route -> v2 runtime
- fallback: no header -> v1 for 90d
- canary: 5% traffic to v2 when header present
- metrics: tag traces by Accept-Version header
I'll open infra PR and add smoke tests.

nate: On monitoring: I'll add an 'api.accept_version' tag to traces and create baseline dashboards.

katie: For migrations: product teams need a test harness. Can we expose a staging token that forces header to v2 so they can validate behavior without changing client code?

alex: @nate / @dan can we do a forced-header staging token? That would help QA.

dan: Yes — infra-bot: will create a staging token and post details shortly.

infra-bot: infra-bot: created staging token stg-accept-v2-2026 (expires in 7 days). Use header to exercise v2 routes.

mira: Note: pagination defaults change for some endpoints in v2 (cursor-first instead of page-based). We'll add feature flags in SDK to opt into new pagination while keeping old defaults for the runway.

sarah: I'm QA lead — assigning a focused smoke suite for endpoints impacted by pagination + auth headers. I'll run tests against stg-accept-v2-2026. ETA 48h.

alex: Proposed rollout timeline: 
- Week 0: announce + docs + SDK PRs open
- Week 1: infra roll + header canary traffic
- Week 3: SDK stable release + customer migration guide published
- Day 90: begin v1 decommission window (customers notified 60/30/7 days)
Open to adjustments.

devex: Also will create a short "how to opt out" snippet for the Console and marketplace partners.

mira: PRs are ready for review, pinging @dan for infra annotations (router config, cache compat).

dan: Reviewing now. Heads up: need to ensure KV-cache keying stays compatible when prompt shapes change — adding unit tests to the runtime.

nate: I'll add an alert: if v2 error rate > 2% for 15m during canary, we flip the canary flag off and notify the oncall.

katie: :thumbsup: sounds reasonable.

alex: Quick asks (please confirm by EOD):
- @mira confirm SDK release date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- @dan confirm canary start ts (unix)
- @devex confirm docs first draft link
- @sarah confirm smoke verification checklist link

mira: Targeting 2026-05-18 for SDK stable release.

dan: Canary start ts: 4312400000.

devex: Draft live: https://redwood.internal/docs/migration/v2-evolution-draft (will iterate).

sarah: Checklist: https://redwood.internal/tests/migration-v2-smoke (endpoints + steps added).

alex: Thanks — I'll collect owners into ticket RW-2381 and add acceptance criteria + follow-ups. If anyone hits blocking PR comments, ping me directly.

mira: One more telemetry ask: include client_sdk_version in traces so we can measure adoption vs older SDKs.

nate: Added to the tracing plan.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for header routing on cluster canary-3 at 4312400100.

devex: Reminder: reach out to marketplace partners — some integrations bundle older SDKs and may need manual updates.

katie: I'll loop in support and PS so they can surface customer migration questions.

alex: Great. Closing this thread for quick sync — we'll use RW-2381 for async updates. Thanks everyone :rocket:
